paper.title: Can an Embodied Agent Find Your "Cat-shaped Mug"? LLM-Guided Exploration for Zero-Shot Object Navigation
paper.central_claim: LGX uses an LLM's commonsense scene-context reasoning for sequential exploration and pretrained GLIP grounding to improve zero-shot object navigation SR by over27% relative to OWL-CoW on RoboTHOR, with superior real-world navigation to visually unique targets.

evidence.quote: We achieve state-of-the-art zero-shot object navigation results on RoboTHOR with a success rate (SR) improvement of over 27% over the current baseline of the OWL-ViT CLIP on Wheels (OWL CoW). Furthermore, we study the usage of LLMs for robot navigation and present an analysis
evidence.support_explanation: Original comparative claim; percentage is relative to OWL-CoW, not isolated LLM gain.

evidence.quote: we first extract contextual cues from the scene in the form of object labels or scene captions. Either of these cues are then used to devise a prompt asking the LLM about which how the agent should proceed to explore the environment. The LLM uses its commonsense knowledge about object relationships in the environment to provide the agent with a direction or object for it to move towards. Simultaneously, we use a Vision-Language model, GLIP [ 17 ] to obtain a target object grounding s
evidence.support_explanation: Scene-to-text context conditions frozen LLM direction/object choices; no task-specific retraining.

evidence.quote: An episode is rendered successful if the target object is in the agent’s view while performing rotate-in-place.
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit visual target criterion, not a conventional distance-arrival guarantee.

evidence.quote: It contains 1800 validation episodes with 15 validation environments. 12 different goal object categories are present. Each exploratory turn carries out the scene understanding procedure described earlier in sections III-B and III-C . For each episode, we run LGX for n_{r} exploratory turns or until it detects the target object above the G_{th} threshold. These constraints form the STOP condition. n_{r} is set to 5, given the small environments in RoboTHOR, where the target object is usually within 10 meters of the spawning point. G_{th} is set to 0.85 for RoboTHOR after ablation experiments described in Table I . The exploratory distance e_{d} described in III-D is set to 5 m, ensuring significant changes to the scenery in RoboTHOR after motion. G_{th} SR (%) SPL (%)
evidence.support_explanation: Simulation episode denominator and5-turn/5m/threshold0.85 settings; same validation suite used for threshold development.

signatures.object: Exploration decision in zero-shot object navigation
signatures.information: Rotate-in-place RGB/depth; YOLO detected object labels or BLIP captions plus language target; depth mapping handled by navigation tools, not raw geometry reasoning by LLM.
signatures.operation: Create contextual prompt asking frozen GPT3 which object/direction to explore; convert textual answer to navigation waypoint, choose random direction when output invalid.
signatures.output: Object/direction choice executed by classical depth-costmap ROS navigation.
signatures.conditions: Scene descriptions must preserve useful target-location semantics; object-direction correspondence and safe classical navigation must work.
signatures.feedback: Next rotation exposes new scene context; GLIP detection or turn cap stops episode.
signatures.selection_rule: Static prompt alternatives and threshold selected empirically on validation data; not a self-improving memory.
signatures.data: RoboTHOR1800 validation episodes; prompt analyses subset500 episodes; staged physical target/room setup.
signatures.persistence: Static prompt/threshold and pretrained models; no persistent visited-history, learned updates or retained library.
signatures.later_use: Next exploration turn uses new scene text; does not retain cross-task improvements.
signatures.claimed_effect: More context-sensitive exploration than frontier/random baselines.
signatures.failure_boundary: Plausible semantic location may be wrong; missing history repeats routes; BLIP branch worse than detector-matched frontier.

signatures.information: GLIP grounding score/bounding box, chosen threshold0.85 in simulator; simulator target truth used for evaluation, not to choose exploration.
signatures.operation: Threshold grounding confidence to stop; otherwise explore until5-turn cap. Evaluate whether actual target lies in view.
signatures.output: STOP or next exploration turn, plus externally checked simulator SR/SPL.
signatures.conditions: Detector score must correlate with actual target; success definition is in-view rather than conventional reach-distance criterion.
signatures.feedback: Target-confidence event ends low-level navigation/exploration; false detections can terminate incorrectly.
signatures.selection_rule: Empirical highest-success threshold on RoboTHOR validation; no untouched threshold test identified.
signatures.data: Threshold sweep Table I on same validation set; physical GLIP87.5% detection and8.3% false detection.
signatures.later_use: Repeated static gate for subsequent tasks.
signatures.claimed_effect: Target identity grounding enables described-instance navigation.
signatures.failure_boundary: False positives, target misses and lack of complete physical trial counts; do not treat confidence as objective success.

gap.author_gap: Zero-shot target navigation needs commonsense context-sensitive exploration and detection of visually distinctive language descriptions, not fixed trained object categories.
gap.checked_gap: Target identity and exploration are separable bottlenecks. GLIP improves detector quality substantially; LLM exploration has only a small isolated simulation advantage over GLIP frontier navigation.

lineage.method: CLIP on Wheels/OWL-CoW frontier exploration; open-vocabulary GLIP grounding; classical RTABMAP/move_base navigation
lineage.source_version: 2303.03480v2 related work and method/experiment descriptions; external original versions not independently fixed/read

gap.closest_adjacent: GLIP-on-Wheels is the load-bearing internal control: same detector with frontier exploration. Against this, YOLO+LLM rises33.2→35, BLIP+LLM falls28.46.
gap.residue: A detector can identify the target only when exploration makes it visible; context may guide search but can also hallucinate target location.
gap.stakes: Wrong room choices and false STOP consume limited exploration horizon.
gap.method_response: Textual scene cues feed commonsense direction choice; GLIP supplies target grounding and stop signal; classical tools execute geometry.
gap.remaining_gap: No unseen-development-holdout confirmation, stronger semantic memory or full physical denominator; headline gain conflates detector replacement and exploration.
unresolved: Real percentages do not uniquely establish trial counts; no reverse-engineered denominator used.
External adjacent versions and full novelty claim cannot be checked without prohibited network access.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: LLM chooses object/direction, ROS navigation executes grounded waypoint.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: Not fixed motion-token vocabulary; semantic candidates are scene dependent and low-level reliability remains assumed.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: BLIP image captions become planner observations; YOLO label variant is a different sensor interface.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: Best reported LGX uses object detector labels, not evidence that the VLM-caption interface is superior.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: GLIP confidence or5-turn cap terminates exploration; missing target triggers next decision.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: Not K201 proposal checking: detector autonomously stops rather than checking an LLM STOP request. Proxy is target-in-view, not arrival-distance verification.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E01 (ablation, common_practice).** Hold the frontier backbone fixed and compare the proposed harness with at least one alternative harness or loop organization on the same episodes. For zero-shot VLN-CE the alternative is a rerun of a published zero-shot harness or workflow (2606.10577#s4, 2609.15195#s4) with the same model; for coding agents, a second deployable harness. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness (rather than the model) raises embodied or agentic success.
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a harness (rather than the model) raises embodied or agentic success.
expectations.reason: GLIP-on-Wheels detector-matched frontier and random alternatives exist; interpret35 vs33.2 rather than all35 vs27.5 as LLM effect.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E02 (ablation, common_practice).** Attribute a gain to a harness component only through one-at-a-time toggles (leave-one-out or single add) with the backbone fixed. A cumulative stack (A, then +B, then +C) or a bundle-level comparison does not separate components or their interactions. — _applies when_ a claim that a specific harness component (depth tool, memory, verifier, skill library, plugin, feedback channel) causes the improvement.
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a specific harness component (depth tool, memory, verifier, skill library, plugin, feedback channel) causes the improvement.
expectations.reason: Detector and exploration alternatives expose component confound; no paired repeated significance for1.8pp and no full loop/memory/termination isolation.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E04 (reproducibility, common_practice).** Report run-to-run variance and use paired task-level statistics: repeated runs per setting, bootstrap or permutation CIs over tasks, and sign tests on discordant episodes. A single run on a 100-episode subset is treated as descriptive. In the read single-run papers, differences of a few points sit within noise. — _applies when_ any success-rate comparison between harnesses, models or training recipes on a fixed task subset.
expectations.applies_when: any success-rate comparison between harnesses, models or training recipes on a fixed task subset.
expectations.reason: 1800 simulator episodes but no repeated-seed uncertainty or paired CIs; real percentages omit definitive per-target trial counts.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E08 (reproducibility, common_practice).** State contamination and development-overlap caveats. Frontier 'zero-shot' describes how the model was used, not what it was trained on. Disclose whether the evaluation tasks were used during harness development, and whether ablations ran under a privileged action space that is not comparable to the benchmark protocol. — _applies when_ a benchmark claim by a frontier-model harness, or ablations run under non-standard execution.
expectations.applies_when: a benchmark claim by a frontier-model harness, or ablations run under non-standard execution.
expectations.reason: Validation threshold sweep and prompt subset analysis disclosed, but same set used for final headline; no clean tuning/test separation or pretraining audit.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E19 (other, common_practice).** Real-robot claims need trial counts and success rates per task. Qualitative demonstrations, or success judged by a human operator without counts, do not support transfer claims. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness or harness-distilled student transfers to a physical robot or aerial vehicle.
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a harness or harness-distilled student transfers to a physical robot or aerial vehicle.
expectations.reason: Physical SR and phase failure rates given; exact trial counts not stated and staged room/object task not independent broad transfer evidence.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E05 (metric, common_practice).** Report cost alongside success: model calls, input and output tokens, wall-clock or per-call latency, and USD per episode or per solved task, including failed trials. Harnesses with similar pass rates can differ about 40x in tokens per solved task. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness, interface or distilled student is better or more practical than an alternative.
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a harness, interface or distilled student is better or more practical than an alternative.
expectations.reason: 5 exploration turns and5m steps define cap, but no tokens/call latency/financial cost of GPT3+perception+navigation.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E16 (metric, common_practice).** Break failures down by endpoint as well as SR: never reached vs reached but wrong stop (the OSR-SR gap), false completion declarations, stuck or no-progress runs, and per-task repeat patterns. Stopping is the dominant residual failure in the read navigation papers. — _applies when_ an embodied navigation or manipulation agent's success claim, especially one that adds a stop or completion check.
expectations.applies_when: an embodied navigation or manipulation agent's success claim, especially one that adds a stop or completion check.
expectations.reason: Physical phase1/phase2 localization failures and detector false positives disclosed; full reached-vs-wrong-stop and repeated-task distributions absent.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E06 (dataset, common_practice).** For a VLN-CE harness, report SR, SPL, OSR and NE on R2R-CE val_unseen, either on the shared 100-episode zero-shot subset or the full split. State which one, and do not mix subset results with full-split numbers of trained methods as if they were matched. — _applies when_ an empirical claim about a zero-shot or harness-based VLN-CE / ObjectNav agent.
expectations.applies_when: an empirical claim about a zero-shot or harness-based VLN-CE / ObjectNav agent.
expectations.reason: Paper is RoboTHOR described-instance ObjectNav, not R2R-CE instruction following. Use stated RoboTHOR SR/SPL and explicit in-view criterion; requiring later R2R-CE splits would change its task rather than validate it.

claims.text: Over27% relative SR gain vs OWL-CoW.
claims.setting: RoboTHOR1800 validation episodes/15 environments/12 goal categories
claims.data_budget: 5 turns,5m exploration; threshold0.85 selected on same validation suite
claims.selection_vs_test: Validation threshold/prompt analyses overlap reported evaluation; no untouched final test
claims.result: (35−27.5)/27.5≈27.3% relative headline; detector-matched LLM exploration gain1.8pp, BLIP variant−4.74pp
claims.denominator: 1800 simulator episodes stated, no repeated-seed execution per episode
claims.counterevidence: Detector substitution carries most headline improvement; small exploration delta without CIs; criterion target-in-view not generic arrival.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Observed overall system improvement on development-used RoboTHOR validation; small, unconfirmed isolated LLM exploration contribution.

claims.data_budget: Eight described target examples; supplied/common room objects; no complete per-task rollout counts
claims.selection_vs_test: Controlled laboratory room/target arrangement, no untouched construction-time holdout established
claims.result: 54.2% success; GLIP true detection87.5%, false detection8.3%; phase2 wrong-room20.8% reported
claims.denominator: Exact trial counts not explicitly supplied; percentages not converted to invented n
claims.counterevidence: Staged protocol, semantic prior errors and detector false positives; no variance/CI.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Reported success in a controlled robot setup, not quantified broad reliable real-world transfer.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported RoboTHOR closed-loop validation success improves from detector-matched frontier33.2 to YOLO-LGX35.0; controlled robot experiments report54.2%, but incomplete physical denominators and tuning overlap prevent broad transfer and large isolated-LLM-gain claims.
unresolved: Physical per-task trial counts and repeated-run uncertainty not disclosed.
No clean selection/test separation for threshold/prompt development.
Target-in-view criterion must not be translated into standard distance-based arrival.
Caption-based branch is worse, so VLM text conversion is not established as the winning interface.
No detector-matched paired CI for1.8pp exploration difference.

G.reason: Concrete language-target identity and context-sensitive exploration bottlenecks; nearby detector/frontier methods clear locally, but residual LLM gap partly detector confounded.

M.reason: Scene-text context, semantic choices, geometry tools and target gate form testable response; semantic hallucination, fallback and proxy STOP limit method guarantees.

X.reason: Static observation/choice/navigation/STOP flow and invalid-output fallback reconstructable; no retained loop invented. Metric-depth calibration and stop fidelity not fully tested.

measurement.reason: Explicit in-view simulator truth and1800 episode denominator; real trial counts incomplete and detection imperfect, so anchors-v2 partial-denominator ceiling2.

causality.reason: Detector-matched GLIP frontier reveals only1.8pp LLM effect and caption variant regression; still real component evidence, but no robust causal isolation of the broad headline.

holdout.reason: Same validation set selects threshold and reports result; physical staged setting does not establish untouched broad transfer. 'Zero-shot' is no task-specific model training, not verified no-overlap.

statistics.reason: Simulator count plus physical phase/detector failure percentages but no repeat variance/CIs and incomplete real n; single-shot benchmark evidence remains descriptive.

cost.reason: 5-turn/5m bound makes interaction cap explicit; no actual token/latency/USD or total perception/navigation cost, so not full cost evidence.
